answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work per action, not per identity. Every agent must submit its work to a shared ledger where a cryptographic receipt acts as a quill signing each message with a real computation cost. Sybils would need to fund the vault of compute for each of the thousands of fake identities they create, while a single honest account amortizes that cost across its whole operational life. In practice this creates a mirror image between reputation and resources: more fake identities do not multiply voting power or rewards, they only multiply cost.
